memory.basis: the sizing of the existing reporting-publish root, which holds the same shape of work: one list of the gold table, a thread pool of twelve reads, and one small document per account. The Lambda runtime was not measured here; its first event is the reading.

words: The root reporting-publish-iso declares one yang-lambda function (handler.lambda_handler, python3.12, timeout 900 s, memory 1024 MB, the existing native pyarrow layer through a read-only data source, no reserved concurrency, no environment variable, no schedule), one execution role and one execution policy with exactly six statement ids: a list of the gold returns table and the platinum reporting prefix, a read of the returns table only, the one PutObject on the platinum reporting prefix, a read back of that prefix, the function's own log group, and the assume-role statement. Three checks were run: the root's HCL grades PASS; the real naming gate grades the three names CONFORMANT and the build-only package of the source-map entry, unpacked, passes the publish handler's behaviour check on a fake S3; and the source-map entry pins twelve closure members to ancestor commits with matching hashes. NOT proven: no plan, no apply, no invoke, and the Lambda runtime's memory and time, which the first event will measure.
